title: Jobs indicator shows up even when there are no background jobs
body:
#### Current Behavior
The indicator (✦) shows up when changing directory, even when no jobs in the background. It disappears when you issue other commands or press enter.

#### Expected Behavior
Indicator should not show up.

#### Additional context/Screenshots
Started to happen after installing zoxide, posted the [issue](https://github.com/participant2/zoxide/issues/527) there as well.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12945959/214962969-9b0db685-0510-4404-9ce9-423efd67f21c.mp4


#### Environment
- Starship version: 1.12.0
- Shell type: bash
- Shell version: 5.1.16
- Terminal emulator: xfce4-terminal
- Operating system: Arch Linux

#### Relevant Shell Configuration
```bash
[[ $- != *i* ]] && return
source /usr/share/fzf/completion.bash
source /usr/share/fzf/key-bindings.bash
bind "set completion-ignore-case on"
shopt -s histappend
shopt -s extglob
eval "$(starship init bash)"
eval "$(zoxide init bash)"
export HISTCONTROL=erasedups:ignoreboth
export HISTFILESIZE=10000
export HISTSIZE=10000
```

#### Starship Configuration
```toml
add_newline = false
format = "$directory$git_branch$git_status$cmd_duration$jobs"

[character]
disabled = true

[cmd_duration]
format = "[$duration]($style) "

[directory]
home_symbol = ""

[line_break]
disabled = true
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: I use _zoxide_ as well, and don't have this issue, neither on _Fish_ (my default shell) nor on _Bash_.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@participant6 are you sure this issue is because of zoxide? The only time zoxide starts up a binary is:

- when you make a query
- when you enter a new directory, via zsh's `chpwd_hook`

Both times, it's started up synchronously, so you should not be seeing background job indicators from zoxide.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
I have just started using zoxide and I have this issue - when I change directory, the next starship prompt shows a background job, but pressing enter again shows that job to have gone.

Is there any way to make starship ignore zoxide as a background job?

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
I use zoxide with fish as well and don't see this issue.
I think this issue might manifest if zoxide is initialized after starship is, as is done in the issue author's config.
Please be sure to have starship init be the last line of your shell's config file.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Good point @participant4, I checked my config for both _Fish_ and _Zsh_, and in both _Zoxide_ is initialized before _Starship_.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Can confirm that the issue is gone after swapping the 2 eval lines in my bashrc:
```bash
eval "$(zoxide init bash)"
eval "$(starship init bash)"
```
Might be worth digging into so that the order won't matter for users who installed starship first then zoxide.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: True. @participant4 is there anything we can add to either zoxide or starship to avoid the need for a specific ordering?

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
I have been testing this for a while and I still do get the job indicator after changing directory.

I have starship initialising at the end of `~/.bashrc` and it stops happening when I comment out the zoxide init line.

Is there anything else I can do?

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: I just realised that if also have another rust tool that initialises in the same way, [direnv](https://github.com/direnv/direnv), so I moved that from near the top of my `.bashrc` to the bottom, after zoxide and before starship and it seems to have fixed the problem.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body: I am going to close this as the original issue has been resolved. We can look into making Starship, zoxide, etc don't depend on the specific order but lets create a dedicated ticket for that.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: @participant5 I still believe this should be treated as a bug, I can't see why order of initialization should matter at all here. Would you like me to create a separate issue?

comments.body:
